text:
By Reesha ,
12 hours ago East Wenatchee First Baptist Church Photo Credit Google Street View Washington State is known to be one of the least religious states in America.¬†A recent¬†poll outlined in Virtual Capitalist shows that only 25% of residents surveyed by the Pew Research Center identified as religious.
What are the most popular religions in Washington, and which counties are the most religious?
Answers¬†pulled from a usreligioncensus.org report used U.S. Census data to see which counties have the¬†greatest and least number of residents that attend church services. The results might surprise you.
Inside a Church Photo Credit Karl Fredrickson on Unsplash "Religiousness (is) based on prayer frequency, attendance at religious services, belief in God, and the importance of religion in life. ‚Äì U.S. Religion Census" Biggest Religions in Washington State A religious landscape study conducted by Pew reveals that the largest religions in Washington are:
Non-Religious (38%)
Evangelical (23%)
Catholic (14%)
Other Religion (10%)
Protestant (9%)
Buddhist (3%)
Latter-Day Saints (Mormon) (3%)

Yakima Buddhist Church in Wapato, WA. Photo Credit: Google Street View Download the KIT Mobile App Now Largest Religions in the U.S. Religions with the largest number of followers in the U.S. are:
Catholic Non-denominational Christian Southern Baptist United Methodist Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-Day Saints (Mormon) States that are the most religious include Mississippi, South Carolina, South Dakota, and Louisiana. The least religious are Vermont, New Hampshire, Maine, and Washington D.C.
Least Religious Counties in Washington State Despite their small populations, census data showed Skamania, Jefferson, San Juan, Klickitat, and Kittitas Counties had the least number of residents who go to church.
Now, let‚Äôs explore the ten most religious counties in Washington.
The Most Religious Counties in Washington State Census data shows Washington is one of the least religious states, but it‚Äôs not that simple‚Äîsome folks aren‚Äôt religious at all, while others are very religious. It all just depends on which county you're in. Gallery Credit: Reesha Cosby Ferndale, Washington in Whatcom County, Photo Credit: Elle Cartier on Unsplash 10. Whatcom County Known for Bellingham, the North Cascades, and being right on the Canadian border 9. Kitsap County Known for the Bremerton and Bangor naval bases and easy ferry rides to Seattle. Gig Harbor in Pierce County Photo Credit Peter Robbins on Unsplash 8. Pierce County Known for Tacoma, Joint Base Lewis-McChord, and access to Mount Rainier National Park. Wapato, WA in Yakima County Photo Credit Zane Winter on Unsplash 7. Yakima County Known for apples, hops, wine, and one of the nation‚Äôs richest farming valleys. Pasco WA in Franklin County Photo Credit Gabriel Sanchez on Unsplash 6. Franklin County Known for Pasco, Columbia River views, and strong agriculture in the Tri-Cities area. 5. Grant County Known for the Columbia Basin irrigation project, Moses Lake, and The Gorge Amphitheatre. Prosser in Benton County Photo Credit Bryce Boehler on Unsplash 4. Benton County Known for Richland and Kennewick, Hanford nuclear history, and Red Mountain wine country. Ritzville in Adams County Photo Credit Peter Robbins on Unsplash 3. Adams County Known for vast wheat fields and classic small farm towns like Ritzville. Oak Harbor in Island County Photo Credit Taisia Karaseva on Unsplash 2. Island County Known for Whidbey Island, Deception Pass, and the Whidbey Naval Air Station. Wenatchee in Chelan County Photo Credit Mark Raptapolus on Unsplash 1. Chelan County Known for Lake Chelan, Leavenworth‚Äôs Bavarian village, and Wenatchee apples and for being the most religious county in Washington.
